correctness.rationale: For all \(1<k\le2\), \(0\le\lambda<1\), \(1<\mu\le2-\lambda\) and \(0<\delta<\min\{k-1,\mu-1\}/2\), the right-hand interval absorbs pseudo-orbits once entered. Exact left backward telescoping yields the factor \(1/(k-1)\), while forward right contraction yields \(1/(1-\lambda)\); the bound is the maximum, with no additive crossing penalty. A viable synchronized entry point exists even at the boundary parameters. Two constant pseudo-orbits near the two fixed points prove both lower bounds, establishing equality. A rational checker exercises 840 finite prefixes and 12 fixed-point witnesses; infinite quantification follows only from the analytical proof.

originality.rationale: Oliveira (2026), Theorem 10.5, establishes qualitative shadowing only for the surjective restriction \(\lambda=2-\mu\), \(1<\mu<k<2\), via a nonsharp bound. Bura, Good, and Samuel (2026) establish a transitivity obstruction and a non-surjective example in the boundary subfamily \(\lambda=0\), \(\mu=2\) for specially chosen \(k\). Neither source states the exact modulus throughout the three-parameter gateway class or its \(k+\lambda=2\) transition; searches found no covering implication. General separate scalar expansion/contraction bounds do not establish lossless synchronization at a discontinuous entry time.

value.rationale: The smallest uniform shadowing error is a canonical invariant governing forward numerical pseudo-orbit fidelity. On the entire three-parameter one-gateway class its exact constant does not depend on jump height despite possible discontinuity/non-surjectivity. The phase boundary \(k+\lambda=2\) switches the extremizing mechanism from the repelling fixed point to the attracting fixed point; the original source's surjective restriction occupies only the latter phase. This motivated complete invariant classification is not an arbitrary slice or a numerical margin increment. The non-surjective boundary includes the published Bura–Good–Samuel example, now quantified for all admissible expansion slopes.
